column1: # The named differences between the Rust core's inert rewrite and the bash
# guard's (scripts/measure/core-inert-differential.py). One per line:
#   name  tokens  payload_free  command pattern  reason
# tokens: the directions a difference of this name may carry, from +flag,
# +rec, +deny:readings-disagree (the core's readings hold different values,
# byte for byte, so it sends no rewrite), +undecided; and ~kind where a class
# may also name a row with no direction at all, whose records differ in kind
# alone. No class lists ~kind: such a row is unclassified until one does. A
# `-` direction (a flag or a record the bash guard writes and the core does
# not, a row the bash guard leaves UNDECIDED and the core does not) has no
# name here: the comparison lists it under `decrease:` with what the shells
# show, for the plan owner to judge row by row.
# payload_free: `yes` where the class may stand on a command whose own top
# level hands on no payload in any of the three readings (rule 3 of
# rust/src/inert.rs allows two such classes). A class marked `no` names a row
# only where the three payload counts are known and not all zero.
# A row matches the first class whose tokens hold all of its directions, whose
# payload_free allows it, and whose pattern (a Python regex) finds the command.
# A name says which reading of the bash rewrite the difference comes from. It
# is not evidence that the difference holds: the comparison shows, per row,
# what each side's command does in the shells, and a named row whose npm calls
# are not the command's as written with flags added is red all the same.
# This table names no class the plan owner has not seen; a pattern here is not
# widened and a class is not added without that.
script-payload-read
column5: A script handed to sh -c, bash -c, zsh -c, dash -c, another shell or eval is a payload the core reads at its own top level (Run::payloads, kind S or E), through the quoting the lexer removed. The bash rewrite read only a single-quoted script, or a double-quoted one with no escape and no substitution (its R spans), and put v2.17.2's flag in the rest (U) or none (G). So the core places the flag after the last argument there too, and records unverified or floor where the script's words or its place say so.

column1: nested-brace
column5: A `}` in a substitution body is read where the body is read, at its own top level (R1, R2: tookdaki-20261006-112251, -135807). The bash rewrite read the body with the outer level's bytes, where a nested `}` is a character, and left that install with no flag.

column1: dq-subst-escaped-operator
column5: An escaped operator in a substitution inside double quotes is a word of the body (R3-1, Pq forms: tookdaki-20261006-211048). The bash rewrite's end finder read the escape as the outer level shows it and ended the statement there.

column1: backquote-continuation
column5: A backquote body is read after the shell's own unescaping (`\\` then a newline is a continuation in the body, R3-1 Pb forms). The bash rewrite read the bytes as written and ended the statement at the newline.

column1: end-after-continuation
column5: A `}` after a line continuation closes the group where the lexer says it does (R3-2: N3, N65, T1, LC1, LC2, LC4, LC9). The bash end finder asked the byte before it in the code view again and read the statement on into `--ignore-scripts=false}`.

column1: arith-subst-payload
column5: A command substitution inside an arithmetic expansion is a payload (the lexer's context stack, claudecy 07ab9df). No bash reader read its body (tookdaki-20261006-211048, note 1).

column1: payload-ends-in-continuation
column5: A payload whose body ends in a line continuation keeps its last argument's place (E1, E2, E6). The bash rewrite's offsets awk lost the final newline and read the backslash as a byte of the last word.

column1: readings-place-apart
column5: The core reads each reading's statements from that reading's lexing, so where bash, zsh and dash end a statement or a word apart (a glob group, an extglob, a `}` zsh reads as a group close) its places differ and the readings disagree: the command is UNDECIDED. The bash rewrite's end finder read one place for all three. Nothing runs on the core's side; the shells' argv on the bash side is the evidence. The name holds only where the core's three values are in fact different (the comparison checks the three, not the token alone), and a place that is wrong by a source map or a place computation is a defect, not this class (plan Notes, 2026-10-06 23:5x and 2026-10-07 00:50).

column1: argument-substitution-preserved
column5: One input, adopted by the plan owner on the evidence of witness-remaining2/w4 (2026-10-07). The bash rewrite added a flag inside `$(echo)`, an argument substitution with no install, which changes the npm argument ` npm` into `--ignore-scripts npm` in every shell; the core does not, and keeps the release's end flag, the flag after the verb and the unverified and unread records. Matched only by its conditions in core-inert-differential.py (argument_substitution_preserved): this exact input, the release floor kept, one bash flag missing and inside a substitution body with no npm, the npm calls and their argument values those of the command as written, v2.18.1's flags and record kept. The tokens here are not used to match.

column1: record-added-in-payload
column5: The core counts an install's `npm` as read only where the bash rewrite's own command-word test agrees, read on the cmdword view of the text the install is in. For an install in a substitution body that is the body's own view, where a short zsh loop head or an argument position reads apart from the command's view: the core then writes an unread record the bash rewrite did not. A record added, nothing else.
